title: the override settings are applied only by a SystemContainer, and the monitor keeps its own file
author: Claude-JG
description: The override settings of ~/.exudyn/config.json are read once into exudyn.special.overrideSettings (#2679), but only a SystemContainer applies the stored visualizationSettings - through a Python subclass installed in __init__.py - so a structure created by exu.VisualizationSettings() gets nothing, and a script that edits one before creating a container sees the defaults. The maintainer wrote the workflow out on 2026-09-26: read the whole file at import, apply what can be applied at once (exudyn.config), keep the rest in exudyn.special.overrideSettings, and apply the visualizationSettings whenever such a structure is CREATED. A Python subclass of VisualizationSettings does that, and it has a trap that has to be closed in the same change: settingsUtilities.DefaultSettingsDictionary(structure) calls type(structure)(), so on an instance of the subclass it would return the OVERRIDDEN value as the default - measured: openGL.multiSampling reads 4 as its own default - which would silently break the dialog's 'diff to default' and Store(SC). It has to construct the compiled base class instead. The results monitor also still keeps a file of its own, ~/.exudyn/resultsMonitor.json. The maintainer deleted it on 2026-09-26 and decided it shall not be used again: the monitor reads and writes the resultsMonitor section of the one file, and the old name disappears from the documentation. The finished workflow goes into the documentation, under the Exudyn module where the override settings are documented (#2680), because a mechanism that is not written down is a mechanism nobody uses on purpose. revision2026b step RG12.10.
releaseNotes: A stored visualizationSetting now reaches EVERY VisualizationSettings structure when it is created - the one a SystemContainer builds and one built by exu.VisualizationSettings(), which got nothing before - through two small subclasses that 'import exudyn' installs only when the file holds such a section. The trap that came with them is closed in the same change: settingsUtilities gained CompiledSettingsClass(structure), and DefaultSettingsDictionary uses it, so the defaults of an overridden structure are still the DEFAULTS - constructing type(structure) would have returned the override as its own default (measured: multiSampling 4 as the default of 1) and silently broken every 'diff to default', the dialog's marking and Store(SC). The results monitor has no file of its own any more: LoadSettings and SaveSettings read and write the resultsMonitor section of ~/.exudyn/config.json, SettingsFileName is gone, and ~/.exudyn/resultsMonitor.json is neither read nor written nor mentioned in the documentation. overrideSettings.StoreSection(name, values) is the one writer of a section - the dialogs, the monitor and Store all go through it - and a setting is recorded once however many structures apply it, so Print() says what was stored rather than how many structures exist. The workflow is written down in the Exudyn module page beside the file it describes, in six steps, with the sentence that a stored setting is not a new default. Six new tests.
